_note: English versions of the park's 10 suggested routes. Names and descriptions translated from the Macedonian text in park-map-2020.json; ends are [lat, lon] of each trailhead, taken from the park's start markers.

1.name: Velgoshti - Letnica - Ramne - Ohrid visitor centre
1.text: A west-facing trail with the climbing spread fairly evenly. The lower part is in low vegetation, the upper part in forest. The ground is hard and stony, with lush grass in places. In several places, especially below Letnica and at the spot called Skala, you cross streams that are easy to cross for most of the year.

2.name: Ramne - Letnica - Visok Vrv - Krstec - Velestovo
2.text: A mostly west-facing trail with the climbing spread fairly evenly. Parts are in low vegetation, higher parts in forest, and the highest stretch is open ground with wide views. The ground is hard and stony, grassy in places. In several places, especially below Letnica and at Skala, you cross streams that are easy to cross for most of the year.

3.name: Velestovo - Krstec - Tri Mazhi peak - Studino - Elshani
3.text: A long combined tour through nearly every kind of habitat in the park. The start and the end face west; higher up you walk along ridges, through dense belts of forest and across wide open karst fields. You gain most of the height at the start, and after that the ups and downs are gentle enough for relaxed walking. The ground is hard and stony, grassy in places. On the ridge path from Krstec to Cresha it's firm earth and stones, and the middle section is mostly rocky. Excellent views over all of Galičica and the wider region.

4.name: Elshani - Bugarska Chuka - Lako Signoj - Galičica pass
4.text: Mostly a ridge walk, and mostly on soft ground that's pleasant underfoot, except from Elshani up to Bugarska Chuka, where it's hard and stony. Apart from short stretches above Elshani there's no vegetation along the path. For most of the way the trail is clear and, in good visibility, easy to follow. Along the way are many historic sites, mostly from the First World War. The park calls it one of the most attractive trails in Macedonia, for the sense of space and the views.

5.name: Galičica pass - Magaro peak - Galičica pass
5.text: Mostly a ridge walk on hard, stony ground. Through the beech forest the path is well cleared; above it there's no vegetation along the path. For most of the way the trail is clear and, in good visibility, easy to follow. Above the forest the trail is a loop past nearly every landform in this part of the mountain. The park recommends going up from the west along the eastern ridge, past the big metal radio reflector, and coming down the south side through the stony dry valley. Along the trail are many First World War sites. It's in the strict protection zone, so you can't leave the trail.

6.name: Dva Javora - Sharbojca house - Samotska Dupka cave - Velestovo
6.text: You cross the middle of the mountain on very gentle terrain, the ups and downs almost level with the contour lines. The ground is mostly hard and stony, with soft grass in parts of the karst fields. There's no vegetation along the path except short stretches near Samotska Dupka cave. For most of the way the trail is clear and, in good visibility, easy to follow.

7.name: Velestovo - Elen Vrv - Konjsko - Elshani
7.text: A west-facing trail with the climbing spread fairly evenly. The ground is hard and stony, grassy in places.

8.name: Peshtani - St Spas - Galičica pass - Peshtani
8.text: A west-facing trail with fairly even, steady climbing that the park calls distinctly sporty. The lower part is in low vegetation, the upper part in forest. The ground is hard and stony, grassy in places.

9.name: Oteshevo - Goga peak - Sharbojca mountain house
9.text: You cross the eastern and central parts of the mountain, with steady climbs and a strongly sporty character. The ground is mostly hard and stony, with soft grass in parts of the karst fields. In its lower half the path is in dense tall forest, easy to walk, though in places there are big fallen trunks across it. For most of the way the trail is clear and, in good visibility, easy to follow.

10.name: Stenje - Konjsko along Lake Prespa
10.text: You follow the shore of Lake Prespa on stony, hard but mostly pleasant ground. Since the path is right along the shoreline, the ups and downs are insignificant. The path is often overgrown with low vegetation on either side, so in places you may have to push through, mostly through grass.

start_fix._note: Park start markers that don't match the start they're labelled with. Index = variant (0 or 1).
